text: Cautions and errors now differ by shape as well as colour (a dashed ring or a solid dot), so they stay clear with colour blindness.
No platform is picked for you: until you choose one, the file is a plain CSV, which also covers platforms not on the list.
Small fixes: Webflow’s own redirect export loads back in, wildcards included, and the notes under each row are shorter, saying only what that row needs.
jsal.io now runs on Cloudflare instead of GitHub Pages: the same pages at the same addresses, quicker to open, and [Privacy](/privacy/) says so.
Spacing follows one scale on every page: a little tighter inside buttons and rows, a little more room between sections.
Five new achievements, each with its trophy: checking a second platform, sharing a result, a batch of ten images, WordPress blocks, and a secret one.
Redirect Import gets its own home page tile, where each address is checked and lands in the file, and Updates runs along the bottom.
Your sheet survives a reload, chains are marked, the file can be renamed and shows each line’s sheet row, and anything off your platform’s help page is flagged.

short: New tool icons and bigger pictures
text: New tool icons, and home tiles that show each tool at work: the CMS Picker’s keys pick a fit, Clean Paste turns text into HTML.
Small fixes: printouts show the page’s address, the 404’s i drops its dot, the analytics card opens by its button, and nothing scrolls sideways.

short: New: a sheet to a redirect file
text: A new tool: paste or drop a sheet of old and new addresses and get the redirect file your platform imports, checked first.
Tick every need you have from day one, such as bookings and selling online, instead of picking just one.
The quiz now suggests Shopify, not only BigCommerce, for shops selling to other businesses (B2B).

short: A WoW bag, real icons and trophies
text: The Backpack is a classic WoW bag with Blizzard’s own icons, each achievement you earn drops a trophy into it, and achievements are grouped by tool.

Small fixes: the HubSpot tick asks whether you pay for HubSpot, Drupal no longer comes up for local businesses, changing an answer shows even rows, every platform’s notes use plainer words, and store costs for Framer, Ghost and HubSpot now include the Shopify shop they sell through.
Moving a site? The quiz now says when staying put fits as well, and ranks platforms that can’t keep your old links working lower.

short: A new home page: each tool at a glance
text: A new home page: each tool shows a working piece of itself, which plays when you point at it.

Small fixes: one name for Off the clock, my WoW UI is now jsal.ui, a one-line Playbook tile, shorter footers, clearer dark tiles, a one-row top bar on phones, a logo menu that fits a phone on its side, bigger tap areas, the Image Resizer’s icon in teal, a plainer logo menu, text in fewer sizes with every section heading matching, pages that open faster in Brave and Firefox, and one gold outline (not two) on a text box you’re typing in.
Substack (paid newsletters) and Square Online (shops and cafés on Square) join the 14 platforms compared; Magento 2 leaves.

short: The need you pick now comes first
text: The need you pick comes first: a platform with it built in now ranks ahead of one that needs an add-on, and a match that lacks it sits under a divider saying so (or a note, when none has it).
HubSpot CMS is a match only when you tick “We already use HubSpot”, as its own card says it suits people already on HubSpot.
A platform now suits your kind of business only where its own card says so, and agency- or developer-built sites count WordPress’s managed hosting as handled.
Results explain themselves in plain words: what you said, what decided a close call, and where the comparison table sets two platforms apart.
Under your best match, say whether you’d pick it, or which you’d pick instead, anonymously, so the quiz can get better (and earn “Two cents”).
“Moving from somewhere?” asks yes or no first; yes opens the list of platforms, with “Somewhere else” at the end.
Results open with a clear verdict on how far ahead the first match is, and your answers sit in tidy tiles, one per question.
On phones the comparison is a third shorter: one line per answer, and a tap opens its note in place.

Small fixes: “A close call” sits on one line on phones, comparison answers are corrected against each platform’s own docs, first steps name the site you’re moving from, a shared result keeps “In two or more languages”, shop sizes read “up to a few hundred” or “thousands” of products, starting free says when the free plan can’t use your own domain, platform pages ask “Allow or block AI crawlers” rather than assuming you want to block them, on phones each new question scrolls fully into view and result cards use the full width, “Copy link to this result” says “Link copied” in green and then goes back, and four quiz questions and the result boxes use plainer words.
Small fixes: one Word comment now counts as one, not two, in “Removed … Word comments”.
Each tool has its own icon: beside its name at the top, in the logo menu, on its home page tile and in its tab.
On phones, the browser bar matches the page, and Android home screens get the logo.

short: A logo: the j and its gem
text: A logo: a j with a gold gem. It signs off every page, and on your first visit the j’s dot knocks the gem into place.
The Platform guides show each platform’s logo, and Updates shows each app’s icon.
Small fixes: the logo menu opens sooner and works after Back, every page passes the W3C checker, and pages load lighter.
The quiz comes first; the cards and the comparison table open when you ask, and picking platforms to compare is clearer.
The mouse wheel scrolls the page again over the settings column.
Every answer and source was rechecked against each platform’s own documentation.
The home page is just the tools, with a guide for each platform, a short Updates list and this changelog.
“Had a platform in mind?” ranks any platform for your answers, and the “Also worth a look” names open it.

short: Languages as a tick; fewer joint results
text: A new quiz: what you need from day one, whether you’re moving platforms, and languages as a tick. Eight questions at most.
Moving between pages is one quiet slide, with the top bar and everything under it staying put.
Results say how close the call was, break ties by what you’re making, and link each reason to its source.
Comparing from a result carries it into the table: each fit, why the best match won, and rows you don’t need dimmed.

short: Terracotta warnings; a firmer light mode
text: Warnings are terracotta, and light mode is firmer, with livelier greens, blues and reds.

short: Its own page: WoW, my UI, the backpack
text: Its own page: WoW Forever, my game UI, the backpack and the achievements.
A page per platform with where to find each SEO setting, like [Squarespace](/cms-picker/squarespace/).
Results say which of your answers tipped them, what counts against them, and when nothing fits well.
Sanity replaces the general “Headless CMS”, checked against its own docs.
A new question on adding features as your site grows, and a “Sell memberships or paid posts” row.
Each platform card links to its own page; on phones the table folds by group, and the key explains “varies”.

short: Copy says Copied; Clear can be undone
text: The Copy buttons say Copied for a moment, and Clear can be undone (Undo clear, or Ctrl+Z).
The heading and list shortcuts of WordPress and Google Docs; Show makes the line it means easy to spot.
Saves PNG too, lossless and with transparency kept, and warns when an image may look blurry.
Uses far less memory and never overwrites a file when saving to a folder.
A new home page with the CMS Picker up front.
Clearer colours, shorter About sections and accessibility fixes; the tools work better on phones.
Quick clicks through the logo menu no longer get lost; on phones the achievement pop-up sits clear of the buttons.
Find your fit in a few questions, with first steps for each match; change any answer from the results.
[Achievements](/play/#ach-h) for using the tools (and a few secrets), and a [backpack](/play/#hi-h) with where to find me.
Clearer descriptions for each project, and what’s live or coming soon.
New: which CMS fits your business, and what you can change for SEO on each.
Edit links in place, and copy as WordPress blocks.
Fits narrow windows, with a new About section.
New names: Platform Playbook and Clean Paste. Faster first load: the fonts now come from jsal.io.
jsal.io launched.
